verses.1: And David said, “Since there are still those who remain in the house of Saul, I will show them kindnesses in favor of Jonathan.”
verses.2: And in the house of Shaul was a servant whose name was Zivah. They called out to him, “David!” And the king said to him, “You are Zivah’s servant.”
verses.3: And the king said, “I will still go to Sheol, and I will show him God’s kindness.” Then Zibah said to the king, “My son, Neche, my feet are weak.”
verses.4: And the king said to him, “Where is he?” He replied, “He is in the house of Mikir ben Amiyel.”
verses.5: And King David sent for him from the house of Makir, son of Amiel.
verses.6: And Mefiboset, son of Jehonatan, son of Shaul, came before David. He fell on his face, bowed down, and said, “David, Mefiboset says, ‘Be my servant.’”
verses.7: And David said to him, “Do not fear. I will do you a favor in exchange for your help during the time of your father Solomon’s reign. I will give you back all the land of Saul, your father’s kingdom. And you shall eat bread on my altar forever.”
verses.8: And they bowed down and said, “What is your will? Why have you turned your face towards the dead dog?”
verses.9: And the king called Ziba, a young man from Saul’s family. He said to him, “All that belonged to Saul and to his entire household, I have given to your son.”
verses.10: And you served him with all your heart. You and your sons and servants served him. And he became the bread of your lives. They ate from his offerings. His descendants would always eat from his offerings, as an offering to me. And he had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.11: And Tzibah said to the king, “Just as your Majesty commands his servants to do, so shall your servant also do. He will eat from my table, just like one of the king’s sons.”
verses.12: And there was a little boy, whose name was Michah. All the servants in the house of Tziva served him.
verses.13: And Mefiboset sits in Jerusalem. Because on the king’s table, he always eats. And he has two legs.
